alt: A living room at dusk with the lamps lit and all four EARF pieces in Poison: a pair of Tropos speakers glowing like lit green glass, the woofers and their insides showing, with deep green stepped horns, their covers off, each on a stepped plinth with a warm line of light beneath, either side of a low oak credenza with a Mantle record player whose dark deck floats on steel posts over a thin line of warm light; a glowing green Core lamp on a side table at the left; a glowing green Hemisphere pendant over a cognac leather chair at the right; a plain plaster wall behind
notes: Each piece takes its name from the Earth. Tropos is Greek for a turn; the troposphere, the layer of air we live in, is named for it. Core, Mantle and Hemisphere are the planet’s own parts. Here all four share one room at dusk with the lights on, in Poison, one of the eight colors. Tropos is in the line’s final colors: Poison poured a step lighter, over a white lining, so the cabinet reads as lit green glass. Mantle’s deck and the lamps are still in stock Poison here; their match to the speaker’s new green is being checked. It is a render, not a photograph: Tropos with its stepped horn and its cover off, on its lit plinth; Core cordless; Mantle as Strata Float, its deck floating on steel posts over a strip of warm light; Hemisphere with its color outside. A daytime version of the same room exists.

header.title: Four pieces, named for the Earth.
